summary: Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer was term-limited, so the seat was open. Jocelyn Benson (Democrat) defeated John James (Republican).

candidates.name: Jocelyn Benson
candidates.bio: Jocelyn Benson is Michigan's Secretary of State. She ran with Winnie Brinks.

positions.summary: Says her central focus is making Michigan more affordable, including building more housing and making childcare free.
Says she would expand healthcare options in rural areas.
Says she will take Michigan's public schools to the top 10 in the nation.
Says she would take on the utility companies that raise rates.

candidates.name: John James
candidates.bio: John James is the U.S. Representative for Michigan's 10th Congressional District. He ran with Jay DeBoyer.

positions.summary: Says he would eliminate the state income tax over time, starting with an immediate one-quarter cut in income tax burden that he says would come from cutting at least $3 billion in what he calls corporate welfare.
Says he would use price transparency, direct primary care, telehealth, and rural provider recruitment to lower costs and expand access.
Says he would opt Michigan into the federal K-12 Education Freedom Tax Credit, expand charter school options, and make parents' control of their children's education the default.
Says he would repeal PA 235, let nuclear, natural gas, renewables and storage compete on cost and reliability, and hold residential electricity bill growth at or below inflation.
